dimensions.analysis: Before touching code, the candidate read the failing test and diff output, explicitly noting the mismatch between released units (eight) and units still held (five), and then posed the question of whether partially shipped holds should return only unshipped units, resolving it against the spec.

They stated a precise mechanism hypothesis - that the sweep releases the original count instead of the remaining count - before opening the implementation file, which is exactly the level of specificity the bar calls for.

The candidate narrated their reasoning at each step: reading the diff, forming the hypothesis, confirming it against the actual code, and explaining the fix afterward, so the transcript alone tells the story of their path.
The edit made was directly the fix implied by their stated hypothesis - changing the release computation from the original unit count to remaining units - with no scattered or contradictory changes.
After saving the change they re-ran the full test suite and confirmed it passed rather than just assuming the fix worked.
They explicitly articulated the root cause (phantom stock from releasing the original count) and explained why subtracting shipped units resolves it, going beyond just noting the test passed.
